blocks.text: Imlo: qo'shimcha qo'shilganda so'z qanday o'zgaradi

Ingliz tilida so'zga ko'pincha qo'shimcha qo'shiladi: `-s` / `-es`, `-ing`, `-ed`, `-er` / `-est`, `-ly`. Ko'p so'zlarda qo'shimcha shunchaki oxiriga yoziladi: work → work**s**, work**ing**, work**ed**. Lekin ba'zan so'z oxiri o'zgaradi: `e` tushib qoladi (make → mak**ing**), `y` → `i` bo'ladi (study → stud**ied**) yoki undosh ikkilanadi (stop → stop**ped**). O'zbek tilida ham shunday hodisa bor: og'iz → og'**z**im, burun → bur**n**i — qo'shimcha qo'shilganda unli tushib qoladi. Inglizchada qaysi o'zgarish bo'lishini so'zning **oxirgi harflari** belgilaydi.

Qoidalarni tushunish uchun ikki atama kerak. **Unli** harflar: a, e, i, o, u. Qolganlari — **undosh**. `y` harfi so'z oxirida unli kabi ishlaydi, shuning uchun qoidalarda **undosh + y** (study, happy, city) va **unli + y** (play, day, enjoy) alohida ko'riladi.

`-s` ikki joyda kerak: otning ko'pligida (→ 66-dars) va Present Simple da he / she / it bilan (→ 5-dars). Odatda faqat `-s` qo'shiladi. `-s`, `-ss`, `-sh`, `-ch`, `-x` bilan tugagan so'zlarga esa `-es` qo'shiladi — aks holda so'zni aytib bo'lmaydi: «boxs», «watchs». `-o` bilan tugaydigan ba'zi so'zlar ham `-es` oladi.

rows: work → work**s**, book → book**s**, day → day**s**
bus → bus**es**, kiss → kiss**es**, wish → wish**es**, watch → watch**es**, box → box**es**
go → go**es**, do → do**es**, potato → potato**es**, tomato → tomato**es** (lekin photo**s**, piano**s**, radio**s**)
city → cit**ies**, study → stud**ies**, try → tr**ies**, fly → fl**ies**
day → day**s**, play → play**s**, key → key**s**, enjoy → enjoy**s**
leaf → lea**ves**, knife → kni**ves**, wife → wi**ves**, shelf → shel**ves** (lekin roof**s**, chef**s**)

items.text: Put the **knives** and **forks** on the table, please.

blocks.text: 2. y bilan tugaydigan so'zlar

**Undosh + y** bo'lsa, `y` deyarli har doim `i` ga aylanadi: stud**ies**, stud**ied**, happ**ier**, eas**ily**. Yagona istisno — `-ing`: study → study**ing**, chunki «studiing» da ikkita `i` yonma-yon kelib qoladi. **Unli + y** bo'lsa, `y` o'zgarmaydi: play**s**, play**ed**, play**ing**. Uchta noto'g'ri fe'lni alohida eslang: pay → **paid**, say → **said**, lay → **laid**.
3. -ing

Undosh + o'qilmaydigan `e` bilan tugagan fe'llarda `e` tushib qoladi: make → mak**ing**, write → writ**ing**, come → com**ing**, have → hav**ing**. Lekin `-ee` va **be** da `e` qoladi: see → see**ing**, agree → agree**ing**, be → be**ing**. `-ie` bilan tugagan uchta fe'lda `ie` → `y`: die → d**ying**, lie → l**ying**, tie → t**ying**. Undoshning ikkilanishi (stop → stop**ping**) — pastda, 7-qismda.

rows: work → work**ing**, read → read**ing**, play → play**ing**, study → study**ing**
make → mak**ing**, write → writ**ing**, come → com**ing**, dance → danc**ing**
see → see**ing**, agree → agree**ing**, be → be**ing**
die → d**ying**, lie → l**ying**, tie → t**ying**
stop → stop**ping**, run → run**ning**, sit → sit**ting**

items.text: Aziz is **writing** a message to his teacher.
We're **having** dinner — can I call you back?
items.translation: Kechki ovqat **qilyapmiz** — keyinroq qo'ng'iroq qilsam maylimi?

items.text: The plants are **dying** because nobody waters them.
items.translation: O'simliklar **qurib qolyapti**, chunki ularni hech kim sug'ormaydi.

blocks.text: 4. -ed

rows: work → work**ed**, clean → clean**ed**, want → want**ed**
live → live**d**, dance → dance**d**, agree → agree**d**, close → close**d**
study → stud**ied**, try → tr**ied**, carry → carr**ied**, cry → cr**ied**
play → play**ed**, enjoy → enjoy**ed**, stay → stay**ed** (istisno: pa**id**, sa**id**)
stop → stop**ped**, plan → plan**ned**, prefer → prefer**red**

blocks.text: 5. -er / -est
Qisqa sifatlarning qiyosiy va orttirma darajasi (→ 87, 90-darslar) hamda «bajaruvchi» ma'nosidagi otlar (run → run**ner**, drive → driv**er**) xuddi shu qoidalar bilan yoziladi.

rows: cheap → cheap**er**, cheap**est**; long → long**er**, long**est**
nice → nice**r**, nice**st**; late → late**r**, late**st**; large → large**r**
happy → happ**ier**, happ**iest**; easy → eas**ier**; busy → bus**ier**; early → earl**ier**
big → big**ger**, big**gest**; hot → hot**ter**; thin → thin**ner**; wet → wet**ter**
run → run**ner**, swim → swim**mer**, drive → driv**er**, begin → begin**ner**

items.text: This is the **easiest** question in the test.

blocks.text: 6. -ly

`-ly` sifatdan ravish yasaydi (→ 86-dars). `-ly` undosh bilan boshlanadi, shuning uchun bu yerda `e` tushmaydi va undosh ikkilanmaydi: nice → nice**ly**, polite → polite**ly**. `-l` bilan tugagan so'zda esa ikkita `l` hosil bo'ladi: careful → careful**ly**, real → real**ly**.

rows: quick → quick**ly**, slow → slow**ly**, nice → nice**ly**, polite → polite**ly**
careful → careful**ly**, real → real**ly**, final → final**ly**, usual → usual**ly**
easy → eas**ily**, happy → happ**ily**, lucky → luck**ily**, angry → angr**ily**
terrible → terrib**ly**, possible → possib**ly**, gentle → gent**ly**, simple → simp**ly**

items.text: Please drive **carefully** — the road is icy.
**Luckily**, nobody was at home when the pipe burst.
items.translation: **Xayriyatki**, quvur yorilganda uyda hech kim yo'q edi.

items.text: I **really** liked the film, but it was **terribly** long.
items.translation: Film menga **juda** yoqdi, lekin **dahshatli darajada** uzun edi.

blocks.text: 7. Undoshning ikkilanishi

Asosiy qoida: so'z **bitta unli + bitta undosh** bilan tugasa (s-t-**o-p**, b-**i-g**, r-**u-n**) va urg'u oxirgi bo'g'inda bo'lsa, unli bilan boshlanadigan qo'shimcha (`-ing`, `-ed`, `-er`, `-est`) oldidan oxirgi undosh ikkilanadi. Nega? Ikkilangan undosh oldingi unli qisqa qolishini ko'rsatadi: hop → hop**ping** («sakramoq»), lekin hope → hop**ing** («umid qilmoq»).

rows: bitta unli + bitta undosh, urg'u oxirgi bo'g'inda
stop → stop**ped**, sit → sit**ting**, big → big**ger**, begin → begin**ning**, prefer → prefer**red**
rain → rain**ing**, cook → cook**ed**, cheap → cheap**er**, wait → wait**ing**
help → help**ed**, start → start**ing**, fast → fast**er**, work → work**ing**
visit → visit**ed**, open → open**ing**, happen → happen**ed**, listen → listen**ing**
snow → snow**ing**, fix → fix**ed**, play → play**er**, new → new**er**

blocks.text: Amerika imlosida `-l` faqat urg'u oxirgi bo'g'inda bo'lsa ikkilanadi: traveled, traveling, canceled. Bizning darslarimiz Britaniya imlosida: travel**led**, cancel**led**.

O'zbeklarning tipik xatolari: «writting» → **writing** (write da `e` tushadi, `t` ikkilanmaydi); «comming» → **coming**; «makeing» → **making**; «studing» → **studying** (`-ing` oldidan `y` qoladi); «plaied» → **played**; «stoped» → **stopped**; «begining» → **beginning**; «happyer» → **happier**; «beautifuly» → **beautifully**; «dieing» → **dying**; «tomatos» → **tomatoes**.

Uchta tez tekshiruv: 1) So'z o'qilmaydigan `e` bilan tugaydimi? — unli bilan boshlanadigan qo'shimcha (`-ing`, `-ed`, `-er`) oldidan uni tashlang, `-ly` oldidan qoldiring. 2) Undosh + `y` mi? — `-ing` dan boshqa hamma qo'shimchada `y` → `i`. 3) Oxiri «unli + undosh» va urg'u shu bo'g'indami? — undoshni ikkilang.
Xulosa

examples.title: **-s** or **-es**: watches, goes, boxes
examples.description: `-s`, `-ss`, `-sh`, `-ch`, `-x` va ba'zi `-o` li so'zlarga `-es` qo'shiladi: watch**es**, go**es**, box**es**, potato**es**. Qolganlariga — `-s`.

sentences.text: My grandmother **watches** Turkish series every evening.
sentences.translation: Buvim har kech turk seriallarini **ko'radi**.

sentences.text: Bekzod **goes** to the gym three times a week.
sentences.translation: Bekzod haftasiga uch marta sport zaliga **boradi**.

sentences.text: These two **boxes** are full of old books.
sentences.translation: Bu ikkita **quti** eski kitoblarga to'la.

sentences.text: The number 25 bus **passes** our house every ten minutes.
sentences.translation: 25-avtobus har o'n daqiqada uyimiz yonidan **o'tadi**.

sentences.text: Madina **misses** her family because she studies in London.
sentences.translation: Madina oilasini **sog'inadi**, chunki u Londonda o'qiydi.

sentences.text: How many **potatoes** do we need for the soup?
sentences.translation: Sho'rva uchun nechta **kartoshka** kerak?

sentences.text: Work usually **finishes** at six, but on Fridays we leave earlier.
sentences.translation: Ish odatda soat oltida **tugaydi**, lekin jumada ertaroq ketamiz.

sentences.text: All the **buses** to the airport are full today.
sentences.translation: Bugun aeroportga ketadigan barcha **avtobuslar** to'la.

sentences.text: Tom **fixes** computers for his friends and never takes money.
sentences.translation: Tom do'stlariga kompyuter **tuzatib beradi** va hech qachon pul olmaydi.

sentences.text: The shop sells silk **dresses** and **scarves** from Margilan.
sentences.translation: Do'kon Marg'ilon ipagidan tikilgan **ko'ylaklar** va **ro'mollar** sotadi.

examples.title: **-ies** or **-ys**: cities, studies, plays
examples.description: Undosh + y → `-ies` (city → cit**ies**, study → stud**ies**); unli + y → `-ys` (play → play**s**, key → key**s**, journey → journey**s**).

sentences.text: My sister **studies** medicine in Samarkand.
sentences.translation: Opam Samarqandda tibbiyotni **o'qiydi**.

sentences.text: Tashkent and Samarkand are two of the oldest **cities** in Central Asia.
sentences.translation: Toshkent va Samarqand Markaziy Osiyodagi eng qadimiy **shaharlardan** ikkitasi.

sentences.text: Aziz always **tries** to help his neighbours.
sentences.translation: Aziz doim qo'shnilariga yordam berishga **harakat qiladi**.

sentences.text: The baby **cries** every time the doorbell rings.
sentences.translation: Eshik qo'ng'irog'i har jiringlaganda chaqaloq **yig'laydi**.

sentences.text: Emma **plays** the piano beautifully.
sentences.translation: Emma pianinoni chiroyli **chaladi**.

sentences.text: I can never find my **keys** in the morning.
sentences.translation: Ertalab hech qachon **kalitlarimni** topolmayman.

sentences.text: There are lots of **families** with small children in our building.
sentences.translation: Binomizda kichik bolali **oilalar** ko'p.

sentences.text: Our holiday was only five **days**, but we saw a lot.
sentences.translation: Ta'tilimiz bor-yo'g'i besh **kun** edi, lekin ko'p narsa ko'rdik.

sentences.text: Who **carries** the shopping upstairs in your family?
sentences.translation: Oilangizda xaridlarni yuqoriga kim **olib chiqadi**?

sentences.text: James really **enjoys** his job, but the long **journeys** to work tire him.
sentences.translation: Jeyms ishidan juda **zavq oladi**, lekin ishga uzoq **yo'l yurish** uni charchatadi.

examples.title: **-ing** without **e**: making, coming, dying
examples.description: O'qilmaydigan `e` `-ing` oldidan tushadi (make → mak**ing**), `-ee` va be da qoladi (see**ing**, be**ing**), `-ie` → `-ying` (die → d**ying**).

sentences.text: Dilnoza is **making** plov for twenty guests.
sentences.translation: Dilnoza yigirma mehmon uchun palov **damlayapti**.

sentences.text: Are you **coming** to Aziz's birthday dinner on Friday?
sentences.translation: Juma kuni Azizning tug'ilgan kun kechasiga **kelasizmi**?

sentences.text: I'm **writing** an email to the hotel in Oxford.
sentences.translation: Oksforddagi mehmonxonaga xat **yozyapman**.

sentences.text: Stop **driving** so fast — we're not in a hurry!
sentences.translation: Bunchalik tez **haydamang** — shoshayotganimiz yo'q!

sentences.text: Thank you for **being** so patient with us.
sentences.translation: Bizga shunchalik sabr **qilganingiz** uchun rahmat.

sentences.text: The old man was **lying** on the grass in the sun.
sentences.translation: Chol quyoshda maysa ustida **yotgan edi**.

sentences.text: My phone is **dying** — can I borrow your charger?
sentences.translation: Telefonimning quvvati **tugayapti** — zaryadlovchingni olib tursam maylimi?

sentences.text: We're **seeing** some friends from Bukhara tonight.
sentences.translation: Bugun kechqurun buxorolik do'stlarimiz bilan **ko'rishyapmiz**.

sentences.text: Bekzod is **taking** his driving test tomorrow.
sentences.translation: Bekzod ertaga haydovchilik imtihonini **topshiryapti**.

sentences.text: Everyone is **dancing** and **having** a great time at the wedding.
sentences.translation: To'yda hamma **raqs tushyapti** va ajoyib vaqt **o'tkazyapti**.

examples.title: Double consonants: **stopped**, **running**
examples.description: Bitta unli + bitta undosh (urg'u oxirida) — undosh ikkilanadi: stop**ped**, run**ning**, plan**ned**, begin**ning**, prefer**red**. Britaniyada `-l` ham: travel**led**.

sentences.text: The bus **stopped** suddenly, and everyone fell forward.
sentences.translation: Avtobus to'satdan **to'xtadi** va hamma oldinga yiqilib ketdi.

sentences.text: Aziz goes **running** in the park every morning.
sentences.translation: Aziz har kuni ertalab parkka **yugurishga** chiqadi.

sentences.text: We **planned** our trip to Khiva very carefully.
sentences.translation: Xivaga sayohatimizni juda puxta **rejalashtirdik**.

sentences.text: Is anyone **sitting** here, or is this seat free?
sentences.translation: Bu yerda kimdir **o'tiribdimi** yoki joy bo'shmi?

sentences.text: The children love **swimming** in the lake near the village.
sentences.translation: Bolalar qishloq yaqinidagi ko'lda **cho'milishni** yaxshi ko'rishadi.

sentences.text: It's **getting** dark, so let's go home.
sentences.translation: Qorong'i **tushyapti**, uyga ketaylik.

sentences.text: Sarah **dropped** her phone, and the screen cracked.
sentences.translation: Sara telefonini **tushirib yubordi** va ekrani yorildi.

sentences.text: At the **beginning** of the lesson, the teacher checks our homework.
sentences.translation: Dars **boshida** o'qituvchi uy vazifamizni tekshiradi.

sentences.text: I **preferred** the old flat because it was closer to work.
sentences.translation: Eski kvartira menga **ko'proq yoqardi**, chunki ishga yaqinroq edi.

sentences.text: Last summer we **travelled** around Scotland by train.
sentences.translation: O'tgan yozda poyezdda Shotlandiya bo'ylab **sayohat qildik**.

examples.title: **-ed**: lived, studied, played, visited
examples.description: `-e` li fe'llarga faqat `-d` (live**d**), undosh + y → `-ied` (stud**ied**), unli + y → `-yed` (play**ed**). Urg'u oxirida bo'lmasa, undosh ikkilanmaydi: visit**ed**, open**ed**.

sentences.text: My grandparents **lived** in Bukhara all their lives.
sentences.translation: Bobom va buvim butun umr Buxoroda **yashashgan**.

sentences.text: Madina **studied** hard and passed all her exams.
sentences.translation: Madina qattiq **o'qidi** va barcha imtihonlardan o'tdi.

sentences.text: We **tried** the new Korean restaurant last night.
sentences.translation: Kecha kechqurun yangi koreys restoranini **sinab ko'rdik**.

sentences.text: Tom **carried** the heavy suitcase up to the fourth floor.
sentences.translation: Tom og'ir chamadonni to'rtinchi qavatgacha **ko'tarib chiqdi**.

sentences.text: The children **played** football until it got dark.
sentences.translation: Bolalar qorong'i tushguncha futbol **o'ynashdi**.

sentences.text: Last year we **stayed** with friends in a village near Samarkand.
sentences.translation: O'tgan yili Samarqand yaqinidagi qishloqda do'stlarimiznikida **turdik**.

sentences.text: The little girl **cried** because she had lost her balloon.
sentences.translation: Kichkina qiz sharini yo'qotib qo'ygani uchun **yig'ladi**.

sentences.text: Have you ever **visited** the Tower of London?

sentences.text: Emma **smiled** and **agreed** to help us with the move.

examples.title: **-er** / **-est**: hotter, easier, nicest
examples.description: Qiyosiy va orttirma darajada: `-e` → + `-r` / `-st` (late**r**), undosh + y → `-ier` / `-iest` (eas**ier**), qisqa unli + undosh → ikkilanadi (hot**ter**, big**gest**).

sentences.text: Summers in Tashkent are much **hotter** than in London.

sentences.text: Chorsu is the **biggest** bazaar I've ever seen.
sentences.translation: Chorsu — men ko'rgan **eng katta** bozor.

sentences.text: The second test was **easier** than the first one.
sentences.translation: Ikkinchi test birinchisidan **osonroq** edi.

sentences.text: Today was the **happiest** day of my life!
sentences.translation: Bugun hayotimdagi **eng baxtli** kun bo'ldi!

sentences.text: Can we take a **later** train? I'm not ready yet.
sentences.translation: **Keyinroqdagi** poyezdga chiqsak bo'ladimi? Hali tayyor emasman.

sentences.text: Aziz looks **thinner** since he started running.
sentences.translation: Yugurishni boshlagandan beri Aziz **ozg'inroq** ko'rinadi.

sentences.text: Mornings are **busier** than evenings in our café.

sentences.text: Let's buy the **cheapest** tickets — we only need seats.

sentences.text: Spring came **earlier** this year, and the apricot trees flowered in March.
sentences.translation: Bu yil bahor **ertaroq** keldi, o'rik daraxtlari martdayoq gulladi.

sentences.text: Bekzod is the **fastest runner** in our class.
sentences.translation: Bekzod sinfimizdagi **eng tez yuguruvchi**.

examples.title: **-ly**: easily, carefully, gently
examples.description: Ravish yasash: ko'pincha + `-ly` (slow**ly**, nice**ly**); `-l` → `-lly` (careful**ly**); undosh + y → `-ily` (eas**ily**); `-le` → `-ly` (gent**ly**); `-ic` → `-ically` (basic**ally**).

sentences.translation: Biroz **sekinroq** gapira olasizmi? Men hali ingliz tilini o'rganyapman.

sentences.text: Madina passed her driving test **easily**.

sentences.translation: Jeyms suhbatga **to'liq** tayyorlangan edi va **nihoyat** ishga qabul qilindi.

examples.title: Mixed spelling practice
examples.description: Aralash mustahkamlash: bir gapda bir nechta qoida — `-es`, `-ies`, `-ing`, `-ed`, `-er` / `-est`, `-ly` va undoshning ikkilanishi.
